title: Implement Stage 2 actor service observations
summary: Add behavior-neutral versioned actor service records, bounded aggregation, and a post-service Stage 1 and Stage 2 join while preserving the legacy shard drain and deferring every forceable Stage 2 policy.
planned_changes: Define independent disabled and observe-only actor-service and buffer-copy connection configuration; add versioned immutable observations and fixed-field epoch accumulators; capture existing actor queue, service, wake, work-kind, effect, follow-on, lifecycle, skip, fault, and exact posted-or-servicing connection-contender primitives; retain exact scheduled timer due ticks in inactive compact work-item storage; record scheduled deadline lateness, connection-local inter-service gap, and service-contender count without a runnable, starvation, or fairness claim; preserve unlike actor primitives in a versioned useful-work vector; add and verify a behavior-neutral generation-token repost gate that coalesces concurrent continuation requests, rejects stale tokens, creates one enqueue owner, and fails closed without connecting it to the legacy shard; capture current send-side retry, raw queue, formatting, combination, sent-retention, path-migration retransmission-clone, receive-segment insertion or reuse, and pooled protected-packet construction primitives; keep missing runnable, oldest-item, continuous-runnable, scalar-work-unit, exact-remaining-work, retained-age, pool-outstanding, platform-staging, and kernel-send state explicit; move eligible epoch publication to a versioned post-service boundary after actor publication and resource release; seal Stage 1, actor, and buffer summaries only under exact monotonic join keys; configure one permanent raw-host accumulator for every adaptive execution; retain every actor dispatch in a separate sample-scoped raw stream and validate its exact source-scoped connection-key and service-sequence membership plus contender aggregation in summarized epoch ranges; retain joined rows, compatibility streams, source hashes, validation counts, manifests, and explicit export failures; carry compact non-identity lifetime tokens through each existing observed managed owner and emit exact guarded terminal-release records at authoritative return boundaries, including recovery and hosted endpoint transfer of protected arrays; add machine-readable schemas and semantic validation; test producer and sink neutrality, sequence, aggregation, reset, join rejection, append-only export, timer provenance, service cadence, contender validity, repost transition ownership, transfer, terminal release, ownership, and existing shard correctness.
verification_plan: Build in Release before testing. Run REQ-QUIC-CRT-0181, REQ-QUIC-CRT-0182, REQ-QUIC-CRT-0183, REQ-QUIC-CRT-0184, REQ-QUIC-CRT-0185, REQ-QUIC-CRT-0186, existing shard, deadline, work-item layout, application-send queue, receive-buffer ownership, stream-capacity, flow-control, metrics, cancellation, disposal, retransmission, and terminal tests. Verify vector component preservation plus idle, posted, servicing, repost-requested, stopped, concurrent-request, stale-token, duplicate-token, remaining-work, abandoned-post, and stop transitions without wiring scheduling behavior. Validate actor, buffer construction, buffer release, post-service boundary, unified epoch, raw wrapper, and raw manifest schemas plus semantic count, sequence, legacy-identity, one-varied-axis, capacity, lifetime-token, and join rules. Run manual or nightly cost and allocation checks outside correctness CI before enabling large campaign export. Do not force actor_work_quantum or buffer_copy_coalescing or claim fairness or performance improvement.
out_of_scope: Large campaign execution, dataset normalization, or ML analysis
